Performance marketing

Performance marketing without the agency: paid media judged on enquiries and sales, run by one senior consultant

Performance marketing is the part of marketing you can hold to a number: what an enquiry, a sale or a new customer cost, and whether that was worth paying. UK businesses usually look for a performance marketing agency to run it. This is the same work done by one consultant with 14+ years on the account, across Google, Microsoft and Meta Ads, with the landing pages and the measurement handled by the same person.

What performance marketing means when you are the one paying

The label covers any advertising that is bought and judged on a measurable outcome rather than on reach. In practice, for most UK businesses, it comes down to four things done together.

Paid search

Google Ads and Microsoft Advertising on the searches people make when they are ready to buy or enquire. Where most performance budgets should start. Google Ads → Microsoft Ads →

Shopping and Performance Max

Product listings and Google's automated campaigns for online stores, judged on margin and new customers instead of on the platform's own revenue figure. E-commerce PPC →

Paid social

Meta Ads on Facebook and Instagram for demand that search cannot reach, with remarketing and creative tested against a control. Facebook Ads →

Measurement and pages

Conversion tracking that reaches the enquiry or the order, and a landing page for each intent. Without these two, the rest is only spend. Tracking → Landing pages →

The numbers that make it performance

  • Cost per qualified enquiry, not cost per lead. A form filled in by a student and one filled in by a buyer are the same lead on a dashboard. The report separates them, using what your sales team or your CRM says happened next.
  • Return measured on margin. For a store, revenue reported by the ad platform is reconciled against the orders in the store itself, with returns and product margin taken into account.
  • New customers shown apart from existing ones. Brand searches and remarketing flatter every account. They are reported in their own line so the cost of winning a new customer is visible.
  • Payback over the real sales cycle. A B2B enquiry that closes in ninety days is judged over ninety days, by cohort, not against the month it arrived in.

These numbers depend on measurement that works under UK consent rules: Consent Mode v2, enhanced conversions and, where there is a sales team, offline conversions imported from the CRM. That work is part of the engagement, not an extra.

If your plan depends on an affiliate programme, influencer work or programmatic buying at scale, an agency is the right choice and I will say so on the first call. The longer comparison is on PPC agency vs PPC consultant.

How it starts

  1. You send the form. Roughly what you spend, on which platforms and what is going wrong. I reply personally, saying whether I can help and where I would look first.
  2. A written audit. Read-only access is enough. Findings come in order of what they cost you: tracking first, then wasted spend, then structure. See the PPC audit.
  3. Ongoing management, if the audit shows there is enough to gain. The accounts, tags and pages stay in your name throughout. See PPC management and how fees are set.

Questions people ask before hiring

What is a performance marketing agency?

An agency that runs advertising bought and judged on measurable outcomes, such as enquiries, sales or new customers, rather than on reach or awareness. The channels are usually paid search, shopping, paid social and sometimes affiliates or programmatic display.

Are you a performance marketing agency?

No. This is an independent practice with one senior consultant. The work is the same as the paid search, shopping and paid social side of a performance marketing agency, done by the person you speak to, without an account team in between.

Which channels do you cover?

Google Ads (Search, Shopping, Performance Max, YouTube and Demand Gen), Microsoft Advertising and Meta Ads, with GA4, Tag Manager, Consent Mode v2 and the landing pages that sit under them.

Do you run affiliate, influencer or programmatic campaigns?

No. Those are separate disciplines, and a business that needs them at scale is better served by an agency or a specialist in that channel. I will tell you so before any work starts.

How is performance measured?

On what your business counts: qualified enquiries, booked appointments, orders at their real margin, or pipeline from the CRM. Platform figures are shown next to those numbers, never in place of them.
